title: [CQ-V12b] Dependency projection agreement
description:
Objective: every daemon place that projects whether a prerequisite is ready must give the answer of the ONE shared predicate, and that answer must agree with QA and delivery. This is V12's DoD 2, split out of the epic-final V12 (task-b621ddc9) on 2026-10-29 by architect-e4b7eee0 for size. V12 re-runs this test unchanged.

Background, read at HEAD 2026-10-29:
- state/dependencyUnblock.ts holds dependencyShortfall, isDependencySatisfied, unmetDependsOn and unmetBlockedOnTaskIds.
- unmetDependsOn(state, task) feeds tools/getContext.ts:512 (task.dependsOnUnmet), tools/listTasks.ts:115, tools/searchTasks.ts:167, tools/setTaskDependencies.ts:84, state/resourceStore.ts:73 (grant eligibility) and tools/claimNextTask.ts:243.
- reportBlocked.ts calls isDependencySatisfied directly.
- CQ-V09 (task-af83018e) makes dependencyShortfall and isDependencySatisfied consumer-aware: (state, taskId, consumer?).
- V09's plan passes the consumer only at claimNextTask:243 and reportBlocked:231, 488 and 495. Any site still calling without the consumer would let a strict consumer see a legacy-DONE or missing prerequisite as ready.

Deliverable:
1. A new packages/moe-daemon/src/__acceptance__/dependencyProjection.acceptance.test.ts on CQ-V11's createMcpCaller (src/__acceptance__/mcpCall.ts). It has no imported handlers. It is table-driven over consumer (legacy, strict) by prerequisite state:
   - legacy DONE;
   - strict DONE with and without verified delivery;
   - ARCHIVED with and without retained proof;
   - missing id;
   - not DONE.
   It asserts that these all equal isDependencySatisfied(state, id, consumer): claim_next_task withholding, get_context dependsOnUnmet, the list_tasks and search_tasks dependsOnUnmet counts, set_task_dependencies dependsOnUnmet, report_blocked dependenciesSatisfied, and the auto-unblock of a BLOCKED consumer. A strict prerequisite is satisfied only after a successful qa_approve on its current candidate with complete delivery evidence.
2. Fix every site that disagrees, so it passes the consumer through the shared predicate, never a parallel one. Each fix gets a failing-first row.
3. CQ-V02's hand-forward (comment on V12 by worker-7d158765): state/deliveryProjection.ts checkFor adds the run's `outcome` to latestCheckRun when one is recorded, and no key when it is absent. Test it in state/deliveryProjection.test.ts. The wire change is additive, and JetBrains' Gson ignores unknown keys.

Error handling: an unjudgeable prerequisite stays unmet (fail closed), at every site.

Scope boundaries: no client UI. JetBrains DeliveryPresentation.kt still renders the reported exit code; that follow-up is outside this epic. No new activity event types; ACTIVITY_EVENT_TYPES is mirrored in moe-vscode. Legacy consumers are byte-identical. Serialize with any open task that touches the same files, since C-series tasks edit getContext.ts and claimNextTask.ts. No .moe edits.

Verification command (fresh, exit 0 required): cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test
definitionOfDone: For every consumer (legacy, strict) x prerequisite state (legacy DONE, strict DONE with/without verified delivery, ARCHIVED with/without retained proof, missing id, not DONE), claim_next_task withholding, get_context dependsOnUnmet, list_tasks/search_tasks dependsOnUnmet, set_task_dependencies dependsOnUnmet and report_blocked dependenciesSatisfied all equal isDependencySatisfied(state, id, consumer), proven by src/__acceptance__/dependencyProjection.acceptance.test.ts through createMcpCaller.

A strict prerequisite counts as satisfied, and auto-unblocks a BLOCKED strict consumer, only after qa_approve succeeded on its current candidate with complete delivery evidence, proven in the same file.

Every non-test call of unmetDependsOn, unmetBlockedOnTaskIds, isDependencySatisfied or dependencyShortfall (including resourceStore grant eligibility) passes the consumer task; each site fixed here has a failing-first row in the same file.
latestCheckRun in the delivery projection carries the run's outcome when one is recorded and no outcome key when absent, proven by state/deliveryProjection.test.ts.
Legacy consumers keep today's answers: every pre-existing dependency, unblock, claim and projection test passes unchanged.
Fresh verification `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` exits 0 and its output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.description:
DoD 4, CQ-V02's hand-forward from worker-7d158765's comment on V12: latestCheckRun carries the run's outcome.

Tests first, in packages/moe-daemon/src/state/deliveryProjection.test.ts, reusing the file's existing check fixture:
- O1: a run with outcome 'timeout' at exit 0 projects latestCheckRun toStrictEqual { command, exitCode: 0, source: 'runner-observed', outcome: 'timeout' }.
- O2: a run without an outcome (a legacy row) projects NO outcome key, toStrictEqual today's shape. Every existing latestCheckRun expectation in the file stays unchanged.
- O3: a hand-edited outcome outside CHECK_OUTCOMES (state/checkRunStore.ts), such as 'PASSED' or 7, projects no outcome key. It is display only: gating stays in delivery/policy.ts.

Then packages/moe-daemon/src/state/deliveryProjection.ts:
- TaskDelivery['latestCheckRun'] gains `outcome?: CheckOutcome`;
- checkFor appends `...(CHECK_OUTCOMES.includes(check.outcome as CheckOutcome) ? { outcome: check.outcome } : {})` after source.

Error handling: an unreadable outcome is omitted, never thrown, inside readEvidence's existing guard. The wire change is additive: JetBrains' Gson ignores unknown keys, and no client renders it in this epic (DeliveryPresentation.kt is out of scope). Hold the SCHEMA.md note for V12's docs sweep.

Iterate with `cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/state/deliveryProjection.test.ts`.
implementationPlan.note:
DoD 4 done. checkFor adds `outcome` to latestCheckRun only when the stored value is a CHECK_OUTCOMES member (isCheckOutcome). Otherwise there is no key, never `outcome: undefined`. TaskDelivery.latestCheckRun picks 'source' | 'outcome' as Partial.

Tests in deliveryProjection.test.ts:
- O1: it.each over all 6 CHECK_OUTCOMES at exit 0, toStrictEqual with outcome. All 6 failed red before the fix.
- O2/O3: undefined, null, 'PASSED' and 7 give exactly today's `expected` (toStrictEqual, no outcome key).

Existing expectations are unchanged. Focused run in the Linux snapshot (/tmp/moe-v12b.aEcJAL): deliveryProjection plus src/server, 15 files, 462 passed. SCHEMA.md and MCP_SERVER.md notes are held for V12's docs sweep. Peer dirty paths noted and untouched (CLAUDE.md, docs/*, moe-jetbrains/*, schema.ts, moe-proxy utils.ts, moe-agent.sh, .moe/*).

implementationPlan.description:
Create packages/moe-daemon/src/__acceptance__/dependencyProjection.acceptance.test.ts (DoD 1, 2 and 5). Keep it to about 250 lines, using it.each and one row builder.

These prerequisites are landed by WORKING time; adapt to their landed names and codes:
- V11's createMcpCaller and McpCallError (src/__acceptance__/mcpCall.ts);
- V09's consumer-aware dependencyShortfall, isDependencySatisfied and describeUnmetDependency, its tokens, and its fixture conventions in state/dependencyReadiness.strict.test.ts.
Never import a .test.ts module, because vitest would re-register its suites.

Tool calls: EVERY projection is read through `call` (createMcpCaller(state)), never a handler. Prerequisite and consumer rows are seeded the way V09's strict test seeds them (raw rows plus the candidate, check-run, review and receipt stores), because no tool can mint a historical state. The one exception is DoD 2's approval, which is a real call('moe.qa_approve').

Settings: deliveryPolicy 'local-branch', qualityGate GATE and qualityGateScope 'everyTask'. A strict DONE prerequisite therefore owes `required-check:${GATE}`. Without a gate, a DONE row would owe nothing and the 'without verified delivery' row could not exist.

Each consumer kind is built as V09 builds it:
- strict: resolveTaskDeliveryPolicy is not 'legacy', e.g. a v2 snapshot with deliveryPolicy 'local-branch';
- legacy: deliveryPolicy 'legacy'.

The matrix. Assert BOTH a hard-coded expected value AND equality with isDependencySatisfied(state, prerequisiteId, consumer) (the oracle), so a wrong oracle also fails:
| prerequisite | legacy consumer | strict consumer |
| legacy DONE | met | unmet (legacy-delivery) |
| strict DONE with the gate run on the current candidate's tree | met | met |
| strict DONE without it | unmet | unmet |
| ARCHIVED with retained proof (current candidate, last review approve, receipt) | met | met |
| ARCHIVED without a receipt | met (today: ARCHIVED is not judged) | unmet (archived-without-verified-delivery) |
| missing id (never created) | met (today: gone satisfies) | unmet (prerequisite-missing) |
| not DONE (WORKING) | unmet | unmet |
If V09's landed rules differ, follow V09's landed tests and record the difference in the step note. Never fit the table to a failing site.

The projections for each row are built fresh by the row builder. Each must agree with the expected value:
1. get_context(consumer): task.dependsOnUnmet toStrictEqual (met ? [] : [id]);
2. list_tasks and search_tasks: the consumer summary's dependsOnUnmet === (met ? 0 : 1);
3. set_task_dependencies(consumer, [id]): dependsOnUnmet toStrictEqual as in 1. For the missing-id row it is the landed refusal for an unknown id: assert its exact codeName;
4. claim_next_task:
   - the ranked pool with statuses ['WORKING'] claims the consumer iff met;
   - an explicit taskId claim of an unmet consumer is refused with the landed codeName, DEPENDENCY_EVIDENCE_MISSING where the shortfall is evidence;
5. report_blocked on a second consumer of the same kind, with blockedOnTaskIds [id]: dependenciesSatisfied === met, and the status is BLOCKED iff unmet.

DoD 2, auto-unblock, as its own describe. Strict and legacy BLOCKED consumers wait on these prerequisites:
- P1: a strict REVIEW prerequisite moved to DONE by call('moe.set_task_status') WITHOUT evidence. Both consumers stay BLOCKED.
- P2: a strict REVIEW prerequisite whose current candidate has the gate run and a recorded completion commit, then call('moe.qa_approve', { candidateId, summary }) succeeds. Both consumers return to blockedFromStatus. Before the approval, both projections said unmet.
- P3: a legacy prerequisite moved to DONE. The legacy consumer unblocks; the strict one stays BLOCKED with legacy-delivery.
Await the event-driven unblock the way state/dependencyUnblock.test.ts does.

Error handling: a prerequisite whose evidence cannot be judged (a hand-edited unrecognised deliveryPolicy on the prerequisite) is unmet at every projection for both consumers, which is fail-closed. Add it as one more matrix row.

Iterate with `cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/__acceptance__/dependencyProjection.acceptance.test.ts`.
implementationPlan.note:
New file src/__acceptance__/dependencyProjection.acceptance.test.ts, 268 lines, 13 tests, all green in the snapshot. No tool handler is imported: every projection goes through createMcpCaller. Runner-observed passes use a second caller whose adapter forwards { runner } exactly as WebSocketServer's /runner channel does. The readiness vi.mock is copied from V09, and a row pins that the real assertExecutionProfileReady still refuses.

Matrix, for each of 8 rows x {legacy, strict}: a hard-coded column AND the isDependencySatisfied oracle, set_task_dependencies dependsOnUnmet, get_context dependsOnUnmet, list_tasks and search_tasks counts, report_blocked dependenciesSatisfied plus status, the auto-unblock (runDependencyUnblock) of a BLOCKED consumer, the explicit-claim refusal codeName plus V09 token text, and the ranked WORKING pool claiming exactly the met consumers.

DoD 2:
- P2: the strict binding is live (STEP_ENTRY_IDENTITY_REQUIRED without attemptId); DELIVERY_EVIDENCE_MISSING before the pass with both consumers BLOCKED; after the runner pass a real qa_approve gives DONE and both return to blockedFromStatus.
- P1 (gate passed false/true): set_task_status DONE never releases the strict consumer (approved-review); the legacy one is released only with the pass.
- P3: a legacy prerequisite DONE releases only the legacy consumer; strict lacks verified-local-snapshot.

DIFFERENCES from the plan, following V09 rev 2's landed rules (mem decision-strict-consumer-readiness):
1. Strict means a verified-local consumer profile, not a deliveryPolicy. Live executionProfile is unset (legacy) with deliveryPolicy 'legacy', qualityGate GATE and scope everyTask. 'local-branch' was dropped because it no longer selects strictness; verified-local checks are judged under every policy.
2. Tokens: verified-local-snapshot replaces legacy-delivery, and delivery-receipt replaces archived-without-verified-delivery. prerequisite-missing is as planned.
3. Not DONE uses REVIEW, so the WORKING pool holds only consumers.
4. Missing id: set_task_dependencies refuses INVALID_INPUT (then the edge is seeded raw), and report_blocked answers ignoredBlockedOnTaskIds without recording anything. That is the pre-existing unknown-id input contract, kept byte-identical.
5. Unjudgeable: the prerequisite snapshot has deliveryPolicy 'bogus'. Unmet everywhere for both kinds, and the claim is refused INVALID_INPUT.
6. Strict consumers sit in epic-2, because a solo seat may not claim an epic+status another seat holds (NO_TEAM_MEMBERSHIP).

implementationPlan.description:
DoD 3: an audit plus fixes, in packages/moe-daemon/src/state/dependencyUnblock.ts.

1. List every non-test call of unmetDependsOn, unmetBlockedOnTaskIds, isDependencySatisfied, dependencyShortfall and describeUnmetDependency (`grep -rn` over packages/moe-daemon/src, excluding *.test.ts). Record each site and the consumer it passes in the step note.
   - Expected after V09: unmetDependsOn and unmetBlockedOnTaskIds forward their own task, so these callers inherit the consumer: getContext.ts, listTasks.ts, searchTasks.ts, setTaskDependencies.ts, resourceStore.ts:73 grant eligibility, util/claimEligibility.ts and claimNextTask.ts.
   - claimNextTask.ts:243 and reportBlocked.ts pass it directly.
2. Fix only sites that DROP the consumer, or that the step 2 matrix shows disagreeing. Each fix passes the task through the SAME shared predicate, never a parallel check. Each fixed site gets a failing-first row in dependencyProjection.acceptance.test.ts: show it red before the fix, then green.
   - The most likely remaining site is the blocked-timeout sweep's describeUnmetDependency(state, id) at about line 330. Pass the task, so the #governors alert names the strict token.
   - That fix is wording only. Pin it with one assertion on the alert text in state/dependencyUnblock.test.ts's existing sweep fixture, if it cannot be reached through MCP.
3. Edit a site outside dependencyUnblock.ts only when the audit proves it is needed, and name it in modifiedFiles. Files that open peer tasks are still editing (C-series: getContext.ts, claimNextTask.ts) are refused: report them with moe.report_blocked instead of editing.

Error handling: every site keeps failing closed. A throw from the predicate is unmet, never satisfied. Legacy consumers keep byte-identical answers: every pre-existing dependency, unblock, claim and projection test passes unchanged (DoD 5).

executionContract.intendedBehavior: Every daemon projection of prerequisite readiness gives the shared predicate's consumer-aware answer: claim_next_task withholding, get_context, list_tasks and search_tasks dependsOnUnmet, set_task_dependencies, report_blocked dependenciesSatisfied, and the auto-unblock. A strict consumer is released only by verified delivery, which for a pending prerequisite means a successful qa_approve with complete evidence. latestCheckRun also projects the run's outcome when one is recorded.
acceptanceCriteria: The consumer x prerequisite matrix agrees across every projection, matching both the hard-coded values and isDependencySatisfied(state, id, consumer).
Auto-unblock of a strict consumer happens only after a successful qa_approve on the prerequisite's current candidate.
Every predicate call site passes its consumer, and each fixed site has a failing-first row.
latestCheckRun.outcome is present when one is recorded and absent otherwise.
Legacy answers are unchanged, and cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test exits 0.
invariants: ONE shared predicate, with no parallel readiness check.
Fail closed: an unjudgeable prerequisite is unmet everywhere.
compatibility: latestCheckRun is additive and gains no key for rows without an outcome.
No new activity event types; ACTIVITY_EVENT_TYPES is mirrored in moe-vscode.
approvedScope: state/dependencyUnblock.ts consumer forwarding, only where the audit proves it is dropped
state/deliveryProjection.ts checkFor outcome, and its test
reuse: V09's consumer-aware predicate and its fixture conventions
sourceAssumptions: state/dependencyUnblock.ts: unmetDependsOn and unmetBlockedOnTaskIds take the consumer task.
state/deliveryProjection.ts:57 checkFor projects command, exitCode and source.
The tools listed in the codebase insights read readiness through unmetDependsOn or isDependencySatisfied.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- Importing V11's gatedApproval or V12a's strict scenario: rejected. Both live in test files, and importing one re-registers its suites. Rows are seeded through the stores, as V09's strict test seeds them. Only DoD 2's approval is a real qa_approve.
- Using isDependencySatisfied as the sole oracle: rejected, because a wrong predicate would agree with itself. Each row also carries a hard-coded expected value.
- Patching each projection site: unnecessary. The sites call unmetDependsOn or unmetBlockedOnTaskIds with their own task, and V09 makes those forward it as the consumer. The fix point is dependencyUnblock.ts, plus whatever the audit proves.
planningNotes.risks:
- V09 may land different tokens or seeding conventions. Follow its landed tests, and record any matrix difference in the step note; never fit the table to a failing site.
- Claim and report_blocked mutate rows, so each row needs a fresh builder, and report_blocked uses a second consumer.
- set_task_dependencies refuses unknown ids, so the missing-id row asserts that refusal.
- The event-driven unblock timing: await it as dependencyUnblock.test.ts does.
- C-series tasks edit getContext.ts and claimNextTask.ts. Do not edit them unless the audit proves a dropped consumer, and then report_blocked rather than collide.
- Keep within the 400-net cap.
- Hold the latestCheckRun.outcome docs for V12's sweep.
